newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES EASE IN QUIET TRADE.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES EASE IN QUIET TRADE.

text.p: Short-term trading rates on Zimbabwe's money market were quoted largely easier in quiet trade on Thursday, dealers said.
The market opened short of Z$155.7 million but the central Reserve Bank forecast a surplus of Z$448.4 million by the end of the day, mainly as a result of treasury bill maturities and other inflows.
However, the central bank did not float its usual treasury bill auction, though bills were trading on the secondary market at 24.25 percent, down from Wednesday's 24.9 percent.
Rates for money on call eased to 22 percent from 23.5 percent.

NCD bills with maturity of 30, 60 and 90 days were quoted at 26 percent from 25.75 (buying) and were being sold a percentage point lower at 24 percent. Bank acceptance bills were at 25.5 percent from 25 (buying) and at 24.5 percent from 24.9 percent on the sell side.
